OpenCascade's XCAF makes each representation item a sub-shape label, and specify-core counts each as a part (SOLID, SHELL); the part is the product definition (its PMI's shape aspects name its one product_definition_shape), so haecceity reads one part: the solid's faces numbered as OpenCascade numbers the solid, the other items' faces after them.

haecceity numbers the part's edges as the file has them, one per EDGE_CURVE; 274 edges OpenCascade's import made have no file instance (ShapeFix's seams on periodic faces the file stores without one, the pieces of closed edges such a seam splits, degenerated edges); OpenCascade numbers 16 wireframe curves of the part's shape representation (TRIMMED_CURVE #6519, #7678, #7699, ..., members of a GEOMETRIC_CURVE_SET, bounding no face) as edges; the part's edges are its B-rep's EDGE_CURVEs; OpenCascade lists some loops' edges backwards: its ShapeFix healing reverses a wire where its geometric checks call for it, which a rule on the file's orientation flags reproduces for most loops but not all (haecceity takes a loop's edges in file order, backwards when the bound's orientation differs from the face's same_sense).
